rules: Do not upgrade a secondary reproduction to primary merely because it quotes or closely reproduces institutional wording.
Do not create EVENT identity from an operation, arrest, proceeding or aggregate count.
Do not create a reviewed-event bundle with an approved human-review decision on behalf of the reviewer.

compiler_status.reason: The reviewed-bundle contract encodes an actual human/editor review decision. No synthetic 'approved' decision is minted for real cases solely to exercise the compiler.
compiler_status.next_step: After source resolution and an explicit human review decision, validate the resulting reviewed bundle and run compile:ltceds-reviewed in dry-run mode before any write.

standard_findings.observation: Shatter demonstrates that a source can provide an exact aggregate event count plus a known investigation seed occurrence window and broad areas, without proving that every cluster member occurred in that seed window.
standard_findings.risk_if_unmodelled: A curator may incorrectly assign the seed date/window to the entire cluster or manufacture a representative map point.
standard_findings.provisional_rule: Keep reported_event_count and member identity separate; store seed window/aggregate geography as source-scoped assertions or cluster-scope metadata, never as a synthetic EVENT occurrence date/point.
standard_findings.decision_trigger: Promote to a schema revision if the same pattern recurs in additional series/cluster slots.

standard_findings.observation: Adjacent multiple targets can remain one continuous_episode when time, place and criminal transaction are uninterrupted.
A high-authority primary source can still be too coarse to create an EVENT. Artemis II validates the separation between source authority and event-level granularity.
Later judgments must remain procedural developments attached to the 1989 event rather than redefining its occurrence date or minting new crime events.
